title: A link-presence test must look at the page body, not the whole page
rule: When a test proves that one docs page links to another (a criterion like 'the page is linked from X'), check the body of X (the <main> element, or the Markdown source) for the link, not the whole built page. The Help site's nav links every page from every page, so a whole-page includes() passes even when the body link is gone. Prove the test by removing the link and seeing it fail.
rationale: E28.3 (#181): the site test checked href="<page>.html" over the whole built page; the nav satisfied it, so removing the in-body links from sources.md and getting-started.md left the suite green.
